title: Sagebrush tags v1
$comment: IDs are immutable opaque identities, never names or filesystem paths. global is an ordinary opt-in display name: it confers no implicit membership. Enabled IDs are strictly ascending (an additional runtime constraint). Validate the complete enclosing grant/reload record against its 4096-byte encoded limit; the tag field alone cannot guarantee that fit.

id.$comment: 128 random bits encoded as lowercase RFC 4648 base32 without padding: 26 characters, with two zero low bits in the last character. Generation must use cryptographic randomness; validation cannot prove entropy. Person, device, host, agent, tag and grant IDs use this format. Type belongs in the field/envelope, not the ID. Unix users: sb-<id>; tag groups: sbt-<id>; units: sagebrush-agent-<id>.service; directories: /srv/sagebrush/agents/<id>/. Never truncate or translate a display name into an ID.

name.$comment: own is reserved for the private scope; Windows device names are reserved across platforms. Names are display slugs only. Renaming never changes the ID; creating a tag with a deleted name never revives its ID or grants.

enabled.$comment: Strictly ascending ASCII order. No normalization or silent sorting on receipt. An empty list enables no tags.

memory.$comment: Absent memory field means off; present tags:[] means own notes only. Names, including global, are never accepted in this list.
